title: Intermittent soft-throttle 'drip' during traffic spikes causing prolonged ramp to full throughput
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Several customers have reported that after a sudden traffic spike, their requests are not allowed through at the expected rate. Instead of quickly ramping to the provisioned/observed throughput, the system issues small allowances in a steady 'drip' (small increments every 2–5s) for 30–90s before reaching steady-state. This causes timeouts on client-side request bursts and creates significant tail latency for bursty features (batch embeddings, batched chat turns).

Observed behavior and scope:
- Affects per-key and per-org enforcement paths when the incoming demand spikes from near-zero to >5x baseline within a short window (e.g., cold clients or after long idle).
- Present on both hosted and Dedicated nodes in region-us-east-1; not isolated to a single shard.
- Billing/usage counters are updated correctly when tokens are emitted, but customers see degraded effective throughput during the drip window, causing perceived SLA violations.
- Happens ~0.7% of spike events across production traffic; higher for routes with long-tail sequence lengths.

Initial data / signals:
- Enforcer logs show repeated small "emit_tokens" events with identical token_count=16 spaced ~2–4s apart instead of a single larger emit event.
- Lease & shard traces show a small delay (~200–500ms) in route metadata reconciliation on some nodes during failover, but this alone doesn't explain the multi-second drip.
- Token refill/credit-smoothing metric (rate_engine.credit_rehydrate_latency_ms) shows a bimodal distribution with a long tail correlating with drip incidents.
- No corresponding upstream admission control throttles or external circuit breakers triggered.

Hypothesis 1 (primary):
The permissive refill algorithm contains a smoothing/decay term intended to avoid a sudden burst of credits when a shard obtains fresh metadata. Under edge timing (stale remote snapshot + local pending credits), the algorithm clamps refills to a conservative tranche size and re-applies an exponential backoff between tranches, producing the visible multi-second drip. The logic was added to protect backend capacity but disproportionally impacts correctness for low-latency burst clients.

Hypothesis 2 (secondary):
A race between per-route lease refresh and cross-shard aggregated snapshot application causes the local enforcer to believe it should rely on an older remote snapshot rate. When the local pending credits are non-zero, the code path merges snapshots using a minimum or median heuristic, which produces incremental token emission rather than an immediate full refill.

Repro steps (incidents reproduced in lab):
1) Start a traffic generator that is idle for 10+ minutes for a synthetic org/key.
2) Burst >200 RPS for 20s to a rate-limited route with per-route burst allowance configured.
3) Observe enforcer logs and metrics; compare tokens_emitted/sec vs expected capacity.
4) Repeat with a controlled jitter of 100–400ms on metadata propagation to simulate shard reconciliation delays.

Impact & priority rationale:
- Customer-visible latency and request failures during common bursty patterns (uploads, batched calls).
- Can cause SLO misses on latency-sensitive integrations and increases support tickets that cite perceived throttling even though billing is not undercounting.
- Acts as P0 because it degrades customer experience and can cascade into retries and higher cost.

Proposed immediate mitigation (short-term):
- Tweak smoothing parameters to reduce exponential backoff cap for tranches to 100ms and increase tranche size limit from 16 to 256 tokens for routes with observed low-latency SLAs. Deploy as a feature flag gated to 10% of traffic and a control group of affected customers.

Proposed long-term fix (preferred):
- Remove the "clamp-to-median" merge heuristic. Change the merge logic to prefer the freshest local snapshot when local pending credits exist, and use a max-based refill for the initial ramp for up to N seconds (configurable). Add deterministic safeguards to avoid catastrophic multi-tenant bursts (per-node global cap).
- Add a short-lived optimistic path: if demand > 3x baseline and token pool empty for < 2s, allow a single larger tranche emission up to a configurable fraction of global burst budget.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary: feature-flag smoothing-override to 10% traffic in us-east-1 for 48h, monitor metrics defined below.
2) Widen to 50% after 48h with no regression, then 100% in 72h.
3) Long-term merge and optimistic path implemented behind a separate flag with staged rollout and A/B measurement of ramp-up latency.
4) Backout: revert feature flags or toggle off the new heuristic; previous behavior is preserved by default config.

Metrics to monitor (alerts & dashboards):
- per_key.ramp_up_p50_seconds (new): time from first request in spike to reaching 80% of steady throughput.
- rate_engine.tokens_emitted_per_sec by node, route, key.
- rate_engine.emit_tranche_size distribution.
- infra.retries_per_request and client_observed_timeouts (increase implies regression).
- billing.delta_unbilled_requests_during_drip (to detect divergence in perceived vs allowed requests).

Acceptance criteria:
- p50 ramp_up time reduces by >= 70% across sampled incidents in canary group.
- No increase in overshoot (burst over-allow) incidents; monitor >99.9th percentile for accidental over-allow.
- No increase in billing misattribution incidents; counters should remain consistent.

Notes / open questions:
- Need review from runtime kernel team: will larger early tranches increase peak mem/kv load?
- Edge case: Org-level hierarchical quotas that co-exist with per-route burst budgets — ensure we don't temporarily violate parent quotas when doing optimistic tranches.
- Evaluate whether Dedicated customers with strict isolation should have different defaults.

comments: 2026-02-11 Marcus Nguyen: Reproduced locally with synthetic workload. Confirmed emit_tranche_size locked at 16. Attaching enforcer logs and flame graphs. Next: instrument the refill merge path to log snapshot sources (local vs remote).

2026-02-13 Aisha Patel (PM): Customer A reported 12% error-rate increase during their morning syncs. Flagging as P0. Coordinate communications with Support to acknowledge investigation. Pending: decide whether to enable short-term smoothing tweak today or after more telemetry.

2026-02-16 Sophia Rivera (SRE): Canary cluster prepared in us-east-1. Added synthetic spike job that runs every 6h to catch regressions. Alert rule added: per_key.ramp_up_p50_seconds > 6s for 5m triggers pager.

2026-02-20 Marcus Nguyen: Deployed smoothing-override flag to 5% of traffic for one day. Early results: ramp_up_p50 down 40% for canary keys, no overshoot observed. Need longer run and more routes (embedding vs chat).

2026-02-25 Marcus Nguyen: Implemented detailed merge logging in PR #1987. Observed that during several incidents the node treated a slightly-stale remote snapshot as authoritative because local pending_credit metadata was missing a timestamp. Fix candidate: ensure pending_credit carries fresh_ts and prefer local when fresh_ts within 1s. Adding unit tests.
2026-03-01 Aisha Patel: Moving issue to In Progress. Prepare customer-facing blurb for Support (what happened, mitigation, ETA for full fix).
recommended_fix: Prefer freshest local snapshot when local pending credits exist; replace median/min merge with conservative max-based initial refill and configurable optimistic tranche. Add unit and integration tests that simulate metadata jitter and validate immediate ramp behavior. Tune tranche caps by route SLA tier.
test_plan: Unit tests for merge logic: deterministic snapshots (local fresh vs remote stale) should prefer local when fresh_ts within threshold.
Integration: synthetic spike harness running across canary nodes to measure ramp_up_p50 under jittered metadata propagation.
Chaos: introduce metadata propagation delays and verify no excessive over-allow across tenants.
Load test: 2h run at synthetic 10k RPS bursts to ensure kernel memory & KV pressure remain acceptable with larger tranches.
